finding: Generic Lynparza can be approved from September 2027 at the earliest, when the olaparib compound patent expires (none of the four filers challenges it); actual US entry depends on drug-product patents running to 2029 that are in litigation with no trial date, and a six-month pediatric exclusivity grant (10-K p.14 footnote 7) would move the earliest date to about March 2028. Merck's $683M US Lynparza profit share (2025) is therefore exposed from late 2027 at the earliest. Lynparza is never mentioned on Merck's four calls, and Merck's LOE commentary names only Januvia, Bridion, Dificid and Keytruda.

Alliance revenue is Merck's half of profits after cost of sales and commercialization (10-Q p.8), so it falls to operating income. FLOOR-DATE SCENARIO, NOT A FORECAST: September 2027 is the earliest FDA approval date, not an expected launch date, and the figures below stack three conditions (entry at the floor date, an at-risk or settled launch, 80% first-year erosion). Date evidence in the corpus: compound patent expires September 2027 and no filer challenges it (10-Q p.22); the 10-K patent table lists Lynparza US 2027 with footnote (7) 'Eligible for six months pediatric market exclusivity' (10-K p.14), so a grant would move the earliest date to about March 2028; the New Jersey suits assert other Orange-Book listed patents, with trial 'expected in 2026' in the 10-K (p.116) and 'awaiting a trial date' in the 10-Q (p.22), and Cipla filed a second Paragraph IV notice on June 12, 2026 (10-Q p.23). Confirmed in the Orange Book file (data/external/orange_book.zip, patent.txt, NDA 208558, tablets): compound patent 7,449,464 expires Sep 8, 2027 (drug substance and drug product); drug-product patents 11,633,396, 11,975,001, 12,048,695, 12,144,810 and 12,178,816 expire Oct 7, 2029 and 8,475,842 expires Dec 31, 2029; use patents 8,071,579 and 8,143,241 expire Aug 12, 2027, 8,859,562 Aug 4, 2031 and 11,970,530 Oct 25, 2041 (use patents can be carved out of generic labels, so the 2029 product patents are the binding ones). There is no data/corpus/drugs/lynparza folder. Assumption: profit share falls in proportion to first-full-year generic erosion of 80% (base), 90% (bear), 50% (bull, if pediatric exclusivity or the later patents delay entry; if entry slips to late 2029 the 2028 loss is $0). Loss in the first full year of generics: base $630M x 80% = $504M; bear $567M; bull $315M. 2027 partial (mid-September to December, base): about $630M / 12 x 3.5 x 80% = $147M. Separately, the $681M Lynparza milestone intangible (June 30, 2026) is amortized through 2028 regardless (10-Q p.8). Ex-US alliance revenue ($767M in 2025) is outside the window (EU 2029, Japan 2028 to 2029). EPS conversion: pretax $M x (1 - 13.3% tax [2,804 / 21,067, MRK 10-K FY2025 p.77]) / 2,507M diluted shares [18,254 / 7.28, same page].
